text:
dmitri: infra-bot alerted: eu-west-1 GPU pool showing degraded health (high mem pressure, 20% less allocatable). paging policy kicked off.
infra-bot: [ALERT] region=eu-west-1 service=gpu-pool severity=sev2 metric=mem_util pct=92 timeframe=5m link=https://internal.metrics/redwood/eu-west-1/gpu-pool
alice: seeing increased latency spikes for hosted inference in eu-west-1, confirmed. Canary traffic failing 503s intermittently.
nina: starting preliminary failover: preparing traffic-shift runbook. tagging @bob for oncall handoff if we need a multi-region roll.
dmitri: @nina run the gradual shift to eu-west-2, but keep 10% baseline in eu-west-1 for gradual warm cache. Use redwoodctl so autoscaler adjustments are tracked.
nina: running command now: ```redwoodctl traffic shift --from eu-west-1 --to eu-west-2 --initial=30 --hold=5m --final=90 --preserve-cache=10```
carla: @nina add a concurrency cap on eu-west-2 pools while scaling, last time we saw OOMs when traffic doubled. Suggest `--max-inflight=800`
nina: good call. re-running with max inflight: ```redwoodctl traffic shift --from eu-west-1 --to eu-west-2 --initial=30 --hold=5m --final=90 --preserve-cache=10 --max-inflight=800```
bob: getting paged in 2m. prepping to take over if this escalates. What does pager policy say for sev2 region hits?
pagerbot: [POLICY] current: sev2 -> primary oncall + infra-eng channel notify. proposal pending: reduce threshold to 10% alloc drop for auto-page on gpu-pool.
dmitri: we should tweak paging to avoid noisy pages for single host flaps. Proposal: require sustained cluster-level degradation >10m OR >15% alloc drop to auto-page. For shorter bursts send only infra-bot channel alert.
raj: agreed. also add a rule: if traffic shift is in progress, suppress auto-page for the same metric to avoid duplicate interrupts.
alice: ops: I pushed a short patch to the infra-bot rule set (staging) that implements suppression during active traffic-shift tags. test logs look fine.
carla: can we also add an automated runbook link in the page with the traffic shift command and quick rollback steps? Makes handoff smoother.
dmitri: yes, include runbook and the `redwoodctl rollback --to-origin` snippet. Nina, once shift hits final, confirm warm caches on eu-west-2 and then mark incident as mitigated.
nina: shift reached 60% after 12m, errors down ~85%. scaling in eu-west-2 happening as expected.
bob: i'm in. taking over active coordination. @dmitri handing off. I'll own escalation and PD followups.
dmitri: thanks @bob. I'm going offline in 30m but will stay reachable for questions. Change log note: incident-ref=1762000123, action=partial-failover, mitigated-by=traffic-shift.
pagerbot: [ACTION] created PD-INC-4821, escalation route: oncall->eng-lead if not ack in 10m. suppressed duplicate pages during traffic-shift.
carla: postmortem note: track cost delta for the burst to eu-west-2; set alert if cross-region egress or instance-hours deviate by >20% in the next 24h.
raj: quick request: can we have a short play to practice this flow next oncall rotation? real incident felt clunky during handoff.
bob: ack. scheduling a 30m dry-run this week. I'll include pager policy edit and infra-bot suppression test.
dmitri: last: Nina, when you mark mitigated please include timestamp and measured latency P95 before/after in the incident thread.
nina: mitigated at 1762001389. eu-west-1 alloc stable, p95 before=480ms, after=150ms. will open a follow-up doc with cost delta and playbook updates. :thumbsup:
